title: Envelope encryption, plainly
subtitle: Sending petabytes to a key vault won't work. So a small key encrypts the data, and a key you control encrypts that key. Think of the two-envelope courier procedure.

steps.desc: A fresh random **data encryption key** encrypts the data, right next to the data.
A **key encryption key** in the key service encrypts the DEK. The KEK never leaves the key service.
The wrapped DEK sits alongside the ciphertext. The plaintext DEK is thrown away.

steps.key: To read: unwrap via the key service
steps.desc: Send the small wrapped DEK to the key service, get the DEK back **if IAM allows**, decrypt locally.

callout.label: Whoever controls the KEK controls every DEK under it.
callout.text: That's why CMEK gives a kill switch: disable the key and reads fail; destroy it and the data is unrecoverable. But default encryption isn't access control: if IAM lets you read the bucket, the platform decrypts for you.

footer: the key is the control point
